alternatives.name: lead session-start routine
alternatives.what: the harness-lead checks at every session start whether a watcher report is older than seven days and, if so, spawns the watcher(s) as the first act of the session (a duty in .claude/agents/harness-lead.md, optionally backed by a SessionStart hook line in .claude/settings.json that prints the due state)

measured.surface: both files that would carry it -- .claude/agents/harness-lead.md and .claude/settings.json -- are in TSK-0130's forbidden_scope (harness-*.md is G5-1's, settings.json is the repo's registration); the stream can build only a helper script under tools/ the lead would have to run by hand, i.e. the state measured above
measured.in_session_cron: Claude Code's session cron (CronCreate/CronList) lives inside ONE session: the generation-4 log measured 'no scheduled jobs' in a fresh session, and no job of a previous session was there -- it does not outlive the session that created it
measured.cost_per_start: a due check reads radar/ for the newest dated file: milliseconds; the watcher run itself is ~9 min and ~130 k tokens for the codex half (generation-4 log line 649), and it would run inside the user's working session, blocking or competing with it

alternatives.verdict: starts a watcher only when a session starts -- a week with no session is a week with no report, which is the measured history (12 runs in 9 weeks, all human-started); rejected by the implementer

alternatives.name: OS-level weekly task (Windows Task Scheduler) running both watchers headless through the CLI
alternatives.what: tools/radar_trigger.py DECLARES the task (name, weekly trigger, the two `claude -p --agent <watcher>` command lines, StartWhenAvailable, an execution time limit) and can --install / --uninstall / --status / --run-now it through schtasks; the repo carries the definition and the installer, the OS carries the registration; a test reads the declaration against the README's claim and measures --install/--uninstall against the real scheduler on a throwaway task name

measured.headless_agent: `claude -p "..." --agent radar-watcher --max-turns 1 --model sonnet --output-format json` in the g5-ladders worktree: rc 0, result 'pong', num_turns 1, model claude-sonnet-5, 21:22:56 -> 21:23:02 (6 s); the project agent definition loads headless (scratch/probe-agent-headless.json)
measured.scheduled_task: throwaway task TSK-0130-probe, weekly trigger, StartWhenAvailable=True, principal Interactive/Limited/zenti, XML persisted under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks: registered 21:27:07, started on demand, state Ready after 6 s, LastTaskResult=0, output file 'pong' from `claude -p` under cmd.exe, unregistered 21:27:15 and gone (scratch/probe_schtask.ps1, run from its own directory)
measured.not_measured: a host reboot (the registration persists in the OS store, which is what survives a reboot by construction; a real reboot was not run); a run while the user is logged OUT (principal Interactive means the task runs in the logged-on session -- with no logon it waits, StartWhenAvailable fires it at the next logon); the full watcher run under the task (the probe ran a one-turn prompt, not the 9-minute report)

survives.host_reboot: by construction (registration persisted in the OS task store; not rebooted to measure)
survives.a_week_without_a_session: yes while the host is on and the user logged on; a missed slot is caught up at the next logon (StartWhenAvailable, measured readable on the registered task)

alternatives.cost: one host-level registration the user installs once from a shell (`python tools/radar_trigger.py --install`), ~2 x 10 min and ~2 x 130 k tokens per week in the background, plus the test's throwaway registration per test run on Windows (skipped elsewhere with the reason)
alternatives.verdict: recommended by the implementer: it is the only one of the two that produces a report in a week nobody opened a session, and HARNESS_V2_SPEC.md line 911 already chose the same shape for the auditor routine ('ein LOKALER Scheduled Task ... headless claude -p')

question_for_the_user: Wie sollen die beiden Radar-Beobachter jede Woche von selbst starten? (A) Der Projektleiter prüft bei jedem Sitzungsstart, ob ein Bericht älter als sieben Tage ist, und startet sie dann in deiner Sitzung -- läuft nur, wenn du eine Sitzung öffnest. (B) Ein Eintrag in der Windows-Aufgabenplanung startet beide Beobachter wöchentlich im Hintergrund über die Kommandozeile -- läuft auch ohne Sitzung, solange der Rechner an und du angemeldet bist (gemessen: ein Probeeintrag lief und antwortete). Empfehlung: B.
